findings.observation: Boundary owns the explicit permission closure and rejects an empty permission. Each verify saves and restores WinLastError on normal return, false permission and permission exception. invoke checks before the scalar lower call and after normal/throwing return; a valid exceptional postcheck rethrows the identical lower exception, while failed postcheck takes precedence. No mutex spans lower calls, no lower retry or output rollback occurs. The documented interface is scalar-value returning, matching the selected SDK routes.

findings.topic: Three checkpoints close normal-return resolver mutation gap
findings.observation: Selected original_call verifies before touching the virtual provider/raw slot. Resolution runs inside its own try/catch; a throwing resolver receives an exceptional permission check before identical rethrow or invalid-postcondition priority. After successful resolution, Boundary.invoke checks again immediately before SDK invocation and after SDK normal/throwing completion. The middle check is outside SDK try, so a failure never calls SDK and does not execute a redundant SDK postcheck. A resolver that changes FLS and returns normally is rejected before SDK. Actual clean sequences are G,R,G,S,G with owner or G,G,S,G with raw slots, with exactly three FLS reads excluding attach/cleanup.

findings.topic: Actual native exception drain versus poisoned retention
findings.observation: One actual native source factory child writes SDK output then throws a pre-created exception under valid PTD. Its terminal Errors predicate requires the identical exception, exact args/prefix/error, retained code owner, inactive/ready Domain, null FLS and zero native leases before exit201. Five separately manual-admitted children cover SDK null FLS, fresh snapshot mutation, resolver normal-null, resolver throw-null and raw SDK-null. They require poisoned active/not-ready retention, unchanged memory block/free/destruction counts, intact prefix or untouched resolver output, no FLS restoration, no extra read/resolver/SDK call on next rejected invocation and exact error, then exit202..206. These manual poisoned cases do not claim successful cleanup through the native wrapper.

remaining_proof_obligations: Boundary applies when callback_scope is explicitly selected, automatically for the current foreign factory. Direct no-scope legacy/custom Context routes remain outside this checkpoint policy.

Permission checkpoints observe actual FLS identity and the fresh snapshot through the existing B21 contract, not continuous state. Raw PTD free/ABA, inaccurate getters, temporary mutation restored between checks and arbitrary provider/SDK reentry remain unsupported.

An invalid PTD postcondition retains poisoned resources. Manual-admitted poisoned tests terminate after state verification; they do not prove the full native wrapper can unwind unknown PTD into successful cleanup or a normal API return.

B23 code-owner retention, slot seal/identity, controller-only setup and sticky mismatch stop remain necessary. Generic shared token and slot integers do not prove code provenance, module pinning, hook success, original ABI or protection from explicit engine uninitialize/unload.

No checkpoint holds a mutex across original SDK execution. Existing single-active admission, same-Execution publication, exact managed shared stream and owned compiler-provider constraints still apply; remaining provider/fallback synchronization is not inferred.
Boundary template is documented for scalar value-returning routes. No generic void/reference/nontrivial-result provider interface is promised by these tests.
Stop/admission counts and code lifetime are not disabled-hook/external-quiescence proof; cached native callback entries and provider unloading still require separate caller guarantees.
